h: Divine Help and the Light of Chanukah

p: רָנִּי וְשִׂמְחִי בַּת צִיּוֹן, כִּי הִנְנִי בָא וְשָׁכַנְתִּי בְתוֹכֵךְ, נְאֻם הַשֵּׁם.
— “Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for behold, I am coming and will dwell in your midst, says Hashem.”

מַה שֶּׁמַּתְחִילִין כָּאן הַהַפְטָרָה, וְהַשַּׁיָּיכוּת לְעִנְיַן הַפְטָרַת חֲנוּכָּה הוּא רַק פְּסוּקֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה, וְלִכְאוֹרָה הָיָה טוֹב יוֹתֵר לְהוֹסִיף הַפְּסוּקִים שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ, שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר גַּם כֵּן בַּמְּנוֹרָה.

— Why is the haftarah begun here? Its connection to the Chanukah haftarah seems to lie only in the verses about the menorah. Seemingly it would have been better to add the subsequent verses, which also discuss the menorah.
אַךְ הַשַּׁיָּיכוּת הוּא מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב רָנִּי וְשִׂמְחִי בַּהוֹוֶה, לָרוֹן וְלִשְׂמוֹחַ תֵּיכֶף, כִּי הִנְנִי בָא בַּהוֹוֶה, דְּלֹא אָמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן עָתִיד.
— The connection, however, is in “Sing and rejoice” in the present: to sing and rejoice immediately, because “behold, I am coming” is also in the present; it is not expressed in the future tense.

h: Joseph and the Holiness of the Covenant

p: וְנִקְרְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּת צִיּוֹן, דְּצִיּוֹן גִּימַטְרִיָּא יוֹסֵף, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא יְתַקֵּן וִיבָרֵר כָּל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּכָל מַאן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִיקְרֵי צַדִּיק.
— Israel are called “daughter of Zion,” for Tziyon has the same numerical value as Joseph. He will repair and refine all the children of Israel, for everyone who is circumcised is called righteous.
וְהַיְינוּ צִיּוֹן, שֶׁמְּצוּיָּנִים בְּאוֹת בְּרִית קוֹדֶשׁ.
— This is “Zion”: they are distinguished by the sign of the holy covenant.
וְאַף בַּפְּגַם שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין יט.) דְּמָשְׁכָה עָרְלָתוֹ וְלֹא מְבַשְׁקַר לֵיהּ,
— Even regarding the flaw discussed in Eruvin (19a), that his foreskin extends and he is not recognized,
יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּרַק אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֵינוֹ מַכִּיר אוֹתוֹ, אֲבָל אַחַר שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה תְשׁוּבָה יְבָרֵר יוֹסֵף אַף אֶת זֶה, כֵּיוָן דְּמָשׁוּךְ דִּינוֹ כְּמָהוּל.

— one can say that only Abraham our father, peace be upon him, does not recognize him. After he repents, however, Joseph will refine even him, since one whose foreskin has been drawn forward is legally considered circumcised.
וּבֶאֱמֶת רְצוֹנֵינוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנֶךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרָכוֹת יז.).
— In truth, “Our desire is to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven in the dough,” etc. (as stated in Berachos 17a).
וְנָשָׂא הַשָּׂעִיר אֶת כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתָם, עֲוֹנוֹת תָּם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סה).
— “The goat shall bear all their iniquities”—the iniquities of the wholesome one (as stated in Bereishis Rabbah, parashah 65).

h: Making the Heart a Dwelling for Hashem

p: וְהִנֵּה חֲנוּכַּת הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים הוּא שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת חֲנוּכַּת הַבַּיִת, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ לִבּוֹ.
— The Hasmonean dedication means that each person can dedicate a house, with Hashem dwelling within his heart.

וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי תִּיקּוּן קְדוּשַׁת הַבְּרִית, בְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף, דְּיָדוּעַ דִּגְזֵרַת הַיְּוָנִים הָיָה תִּיבָּעֵל לְטַפְסָר תְּחִילָּה, שֶׁהַיְּוָנִים רָצוּ לְהַטִּיל זוּהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.

— This comes through repairing the holiness of the covenant, the aspect of Joseph. As is known, the Greek decree required a woman first to submit to intercourse with the governor. The Greeks sought to infuse Israel with the serpent's defilement.
וּכְמוֹ דְּבוֹעֵל אֲרַמִּית מָשְׁכָא עָרְלָתוֹ, כֵּן בְּהֵיפֶךְ כְּתִיב: וַתִּדְבַּק נַפְשׁוֹ בְּדִינָה, וְאִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פ): גּוֹרְרִין בָּהּ וְכוּלֵי, קָשֶׁה לִפְרוֹשׁ.

— Just as intercourse with a gentile woman draws a man's foreskin forward, so in the reverse situation it is written: “His soul clung to Dinah.” It is taught (Bereishis Rabbah, parashah 80): “They dragged her,” etc.; “It is difficult to separate.”
וְהַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים תִּקְּנוּ זֹאת כְּשֶׁנִּצְּחוּם וְקָבְעוּ חֲנוּכָּה, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— The Hasmoneans repaired this when they defeated them and established Chanukah: Hashem dwells among the children of Israel.

וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי הִנְנִי בָא וְשָׁכַנְתִּי בְתוֹכֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר, וְהַיְינוּ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת מְקוֹם מִשְׁכָּן לְהַשֵּׁם וְלַעֲשׂוֹת חֲנוּכַּת הַבַּיִת.
— This is the meaning of “For behold, I am coming and will dwell in your midst,” etc. During those days, every Jew can make a dwelling place for Hashem and celebrate the dedication of the house.

וְכֵן כָּתוּב אַחַר כָּךְ מֵעִנְיַן יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן מֵעֵין פְּגַם זֶה, שֶׁבָּנָיו נָשְׂאוּ נָשִׁים דְּלָא כַשְׁרָן לִכְהוּנְתָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתַּרְגּוּם וּגְמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין צג.).

— The subsequent passage about Yehoshua the High Priest likewise concerns something resembling this flaw: his sons married women unfit for the priesthood, as stated in the Targum and Gemara (Sanhedrin 93a).
וּכְתִיב: וַיָּשִׂימוּ הַצָּנִיף הַטָּהוֹר עַל רֹאשׁוֹ, וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת עז:): סוּדָרָא, סוֹד הַשֵּׁם לִירֵאָיו.
— It is written: “They placed the pure turban upon his head.” This accords with what is said (Shabbat 77b): “Sudara—a cloth: ‘Hashem's secret is for those who fear Him.’”
שֶׁמִּזֶּה שֶׁמְּכַסִּין רֹאשָׁם בְּסוּדָר הַמְיוּחָד לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם, זוֹכִין וּמַשִּׂיגִין סוֹד הַשֵּׁם, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: וְיַחֲזֵי לָן סִתְרֵיהּ דְּאִתְאֲמַר בִּלְחִישָׁא.
— By covering their heads with the cloth distinctive to a Torah scholar, they merit attaining Hashem's secret. As we say: “May He show us His hidden mystery, which is uttered in a whisper.”
וְזֶה סוֹד הַשֵּׁם, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ: מְנוֹרַת זָהָב כּוּלָּהּ וְגוּלָּה עַל רֹאשָׁהּ, עַל דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁהוּא כְּכֶתֶר עַל הָרֹאשׁ.
— This is Hashem's secret. Thus it subsequently says: “A menorah entirely of gold, with its bowl upon its head.” Specifically “upon”: it is like a crown upon the head.
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא (פָּרָשָׁה ח) עַל פָּסוּק זֶה: וַיַּעֲבֹר וְגוֹמֵר וַהַשֵּׁם בְּרֹאשָׁם, דְּקָאֵי עַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
— This is what the Pesikta (section 8) says concerning the verse “He passed, etc., and Hashem at their head”: it refers to the Holy One, blessed be He.
וְכֵן וְשִׁבְעָה נֵרוֹתֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ דַּיְיקָא, וְהַכֹּל לְרֶמֶז זֶה. וּכְתִיב וְשִׁבְעָה מוּצָקוֹת וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁמְּרִיקוֹת הַשֶּׁמֶן מֵעַצְמָן.
— Likewise, “Its seven lamps upon it”—specifically “upon”—all allude to this. It says: “And seven conduits,” etc., which pour the oil of themselves.

h: Might and Power Require Divine Help

p: וּמְסַיֵּים: לֹא בְחַיִל וְלֹא בְכֹחַ כִּי אִם בְּרוּחִי וְגוֹמֵר.
— It concludes: “Not through might and not through power, but through My spirit,” etc.
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: אֵין הַמֶּלֶךְ נוֹשָׁע בְּרָב חָיִל, גִּבּוֹר לֹא יִנָּצֵל בְּרָב כֹּחַ, שֶׁקֶר הַסּוּס וְגוֹמֵר.
— This accords with: “A king is not saved by great might; a warrior is not delivered by great strength. A horse is a false hope,” etc.
חַיִל הַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוֹף בְּרָכוֹת): מֵחַיִל אֶל חָיִל, וּפֵירֵשׁ רַבִּי שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי: מִישִׁיבָה לִישִׁיבָה וְכוּלֵי.
— “Might” means words of Torah, as it says (end of Berachos): “From strength to strength.” Rashi explains: “From one academy to another,” etc.
וְרַבָּנַן אִקְרוּ מְלָכִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: בִּי מְלָכִים יִמְלוֹכוּ (וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גִּיטִּין סב.).
— The sages are called kings, as it says: “Through me kings reign” (as stated in Gittin 62a).
וְאָמַר דְּאַף דְּלֵית לָךְ מִלָּה לְתַבְּרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ,
— It says that although “there is nothing that can break the evil inclination except Torah,” as stated in the holy Zohar on this parashah,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין הַמֶּלֶךְ, שֶׁהוּא הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם, נוֹשָׁע בְּרָב חָיִל, שֶׁדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּעַצְמוֹ לֹא יוֹעִיל לְהִוָּושֵׁעַ מֵהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
— nevertheless “the king,” the Torah scholar, “is not saved by great might.” Words of Torah alone will not suffice to save him from the evil inclination.

וְכֵן גִּבּוֹר, שֶׁהוּא הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ, לֹא יִנָּצֵל בְּרָב כֹּחַ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ יִרְאַת הָאָדָם בְּעַצְמוֹ לֹא יִנָּצֵל מִקִּטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סוּכָּה נב:): וְאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעוֹזֵר לוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ.

— Likewise, the warrior, one who conquers his inclination, “is not delivered by great strength.” The power of a person's awe alone will not deliver him from the evil inclination's accusations. As it says (Sukkah 52b): “Were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to help him, he could not overcome it.”

שֶׁקֶר הַסּוּס לִתְשׁוּעָה, הַיְינוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת, וְזֶה מְכוּנֶּה בְּשֵׁם סוּס, וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין צו.): כְּשֶׁאֲנִי מְשַׁלֵּם שָׂכָר לְאַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁרָצוּ לְפָנַי כַּסּוּסִים וְכוּלֵי.

— “A horse is a false hope for deliverance” refers to effort in performing mitzvos, which is termed a horse. As it says (Sanhedrin 96a): “When I pay the reward of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who ran before Me like horses,” etc.
גַּם זֶה אָמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל לִתְשׁוּעָה מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע. רַק הִנֵּה עֵין הַשֵּׁם אֶל יְרֵאָיו, לַמְיַחֲלִים לְחַסְדּוֹ, שֶׁעוֹזֵר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּחַסְדּוֹ.

— This too, it says, does not suffice for deliverance from the evil inclination. Rather, “Behold, Hashem's eye is upon those who fear Him, upon those who hope for His kindness”: Hashem helps a person through His kindness.

וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: לֹא בְחַיִל וְלֹא בְכֹחַ כִּי אִם בְּרוּחִי וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁאֱמֶת שֶׁחַיִל, שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְכֵן כֹּחַ וּגְבוּרָה לִכְבּוֹשׁ אֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, הֵם עֵצוֹת לְתַבְּרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע וּלְהִנָּצֵל מִקִּטְרוּגוֹ,

— This is the meaning of “Not through might and not through power, but through My spirit,” etc. Indeed, might—words of Torah—and power and strength in conquering the evil inclination are means of breaking it and escaping its accusations.
אֲבָל אֵינָם מוֹעִילִים רַק כְּשֶׁבָּאִין מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְתַבְּרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ בְּעַצְמוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וְגוּלָּה עַל רֹאשָׁהּ, כָּאָמוּר.
— They are effective, however, only when they come from Hashem to break the evil inclination, and Hashem Himself bestows the influence, as in “Its bowl upon its head,” as explained.

Then it concludes, ‘This is the word of Hashem to Zerubavel: Not by might and not by power, but by My spirit, says Hashem of Hosts.’ … Therefore Hashem showed Zechariah at that time that the menorah, the aspect of the light of the Oral Torah, truly comes from Hashem’s side, for the olives pour out the oil of themselves. Jacob said, ‘The God before whom my fathers walked,’ for Abraham and Isaac each served Hashem through his own effort; but of himself he said, ‘The God who has shepherded me,’ for he recognized that even the effort comes from Hashem alone, who shepherds and guides him. … ‘Not by might’ is words of Torah, ‘and not by power’ is the awe that comes through human effort, ‘but by My spirit, says Hashem of Hosts’: this is the Oral Torah, which Hashem bestows of Himself as a gift, as it says, ‘My spirit that is upon you and My words that I have placed in your mouth.’”

h: Wisdom Strength and Wealth as Heavenly Gifts

p: וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (רַבָּה וְתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת מַטּוֹת): שָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת טוֹבוֹת בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּעוֹלָם, חָכְמָה וּגְבוּרָה וְעוֹשֶׁר; זָכָה לְאַחַת מֵהֶן, נוֹטֵל חֶמְדַּת כָּל הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי. אֵימָתַי? בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵם מַתְּנוֹת שָׁמַיִם וְכוּלֵי.

— This is what the Midrash states (Rabbah and Tanchuma, Mattos): “The Holy One, blessed be He, created three good gifts in the world: wisdom, strength, and wealth. One who merits one of them acquires the world's most desirable things, etc. When? When they are gifts from Heaven,” etc.
חָכְמָה הַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה. גְּבוּרָה, יִרְאָה, לִהְיוֹת גִּבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ. עוֹשֶׁר הַיְינוּ בַּעֲלֵי מִצְוֹת גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים,
— Wisdom means words of Torah; strength means awe, being mighty in conquering one's inclination; wealth refers to those who perform mitzvos of acts of kindness.

וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ז): עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת צֵל וְחוּפָּה לְבַעֲלֵי מִצְוֹת אֵצֶל בַּעֲלֵי תוֹרָה. מַאי טַעְמָא? כִּי בְּצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכָּסֶף.

— As it says (Koheles Rabbah, parashah 7): “In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will make shelter and a canopy for those who perform mitzvos beside those who possess Torah.” Why? “For in the shelter of wisdom is the shelter of money.”
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר שֶׁכָּל אֵלּוּ לֹא יוֹעִיל רַק בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵם מַתְּנוֹת שָׁמַיִם וּבָאוֹת מִכֹּחַ הַגְּבוּרָה שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
— Concerning all these, it says that they are effective only when they are gifts from Heaven, coming from the Holy One's power and strength.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ וּמַשְׁפִּיעַ לוֹ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְתַבְּרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע,
— That is, the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him and bestows upon him words of Torah to break the evil inclination.
דְּאִם לֹא כֵּן מָצִינוּ (סוּכָּה נב) שֶׁכָּל הַגָּדוֹל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ יִצְרוֹ גָּדוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ, וְאַבַּיֵּי אָמַר: אִי מַאן דְּסָנוּ לִי וְכוּלֵי.
— For otherwise, we find (Sukkah 52) that “Whoever is greater than his fellow has a greater inclination than he,” and Abaye said: “If the one whom I hate,” etc.
וּגְבוּרַת הָאָדָם אָמְרוּ: אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעוֹזֵר לוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ.
— Regarding human strength they said: “Were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to help him, he could not overcome it.”
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: אַל יִתְהַלֵּל הֶחָכָם בְּחָכְמָתוֹ, רַב חָיִל.
— This is the meaning of “Let not the wise man boast of his wisdom”—great might.
וְאַל יִתְהַלֵּל הַגִּבּוֹר בִּגְבוּרָתוֹ דַּיְיקָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: גִּבּוֹר לֹא יִנָּצֵל בְּרָב כֹּחַ.
— “Let not the strong man boast of his strength”—specifically his own strength—as it says: “A warrior is not delivered by great strength.”

אַל יִתְהַלֵּל עָשִׁיר בְּעָשְׁרוֹ, הַיְינוּ בַּעַל מִצְוֹת גְּמִילוּת חֲסָדִים גַּם כֵּן לֹא יוּכַל לְהִתְהַלֵּל שֶׁיּוּכַל לְנַצֵּחַ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע בִּזְכוּת זֶה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: שֶׁקֶר הַסּוּס לִתְשׁוּעָה, וְאַף תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת גַּם כֵּן לֹא יִמָּלֵט.

— “Let not the rich man boast of his wealth”: one who performs mitzvos of acts of kindness also cannot boast that through this merit he can defeat the evil inclination. As it says: “A horse is a false hope for deliverance.” Even through Torah and mitzvos, he does not thereby escape.
כִּי אִם בְּזֹאת יִתְהַלֵּל, הַשְׂכֵּל וְיָדוֹעַ אוֹתִי, שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִבְחִינַת הַדַּעַת שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי חִבּוּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה, מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא.
— “Rather, let him boast in this: understanding and knowing Me”—attaining the aspect of Daas, which comes through the joining of Chochmah and Binah, mind and heart.
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס הַיִּרְאָה לְמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי תָבוֹא חָכְמָה בְלִבֶּךָ וְדַעַת לְנַפְשְׁךָ יִנְעָם.
— This occurs when awe enters the depths of the heart, as it says: “For wisdom shall enter your heart, and knowledge shall be pleasant to your soul.”

h: A Broken Heart and the Gift of Daas

p: וְכֵן זְרוּבָּבֶל לִבּוֹ נִשְׁבָּר אֵיךְ יִבְנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְאָמַר לוֹ הַנָּבִיא: לֹא בְחַיִל וְלֹא בְכֹחַ כִּי אִם בְּרוּחִי, כְּשֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִבְחִינַת הַדַּעַת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ נִשְׁבָּר וְשָׁפָל בְּעֵינָיו, יִהְיֶה הַשֵּׁם בְּעֶזְרוֹ.

— Likewise, Zerubavel was brokenhearted over how he could build the Temple. The prophet told him: “Not through might and not through power, but through My spirit.” When he attains Daas from Hashem, through his broken heart and humility in his own eyes, Hashem will help him.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: מִי אַתָּה הַר הַגָּדוֹל לִפְנֵי זְרוּבָּבֶל, מְרַמֵּז עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (שָׁם): צַדִּיקִים נִדְמֶה לָהֶם כְּהַר וְכוּלֵי.
— Thus it says: “Who are you, great mountain, before Zerubavel?” It alludes to the evil inclination, as the Gemara states there: “To the righteous it appears like a mountain,” etc.
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשַׁת חֲנוּכָּה, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שָׁפָל בְּעֵינָיו וְיַכִּיר שֶׁהַכֹּל מַתְּנוֹת שָׁמַיִם.
— This too is the root of Chanukah's holiness: being humble in one's own eyes and recognizing that everything is a gift from Heaven.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁעַל זֶה מוֹרֶה שֵׁם מַתִּתְיָהוּ בֶּן יוֹחָנָן, שֶׁהִכִּיר שֶׁהַכֹּל מַתַּת יה״ו, וְהַכֹּל י״ו חָנַן.
— As we explained, the name Mattisyahu ben Yochanan indicates this: he recognized that everything is mattas Y-H-V, a gift from Hashem, and everything is Y-V chanan, graciously bestowed by Hashem.
וּמִי שֶׁמַּכִּיר זֶה וּמְיַיחֵל לְחַסְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, זוֹכֶה לְהַדַּעַת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: הִנֵּה עֵין הַשֵּׁם אֶל יְרֵאָיו, לַמְיַחֲלִים לְחַסְדּוֹ.
— One who recognizes this and hopes for Hashem's kindness merits Daas from Hashem, as it says: “Behold, Hashem's eye is upon those who fear Him, upon those who hope for His kindness.”

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 52a: “R. Judah expounded: In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will bring the evil inclination and slaughter it before the righteous and the wicked. To the righteous it appears like a high mountain, and to the wicked like a strand of hair. Both groups weep. The righteous weep and say, “How were we able to conquer such a high mountain?” The wicked weep and say, “How were we unable to conquer this strand of hair?” The Holy One, blessed be He, also marvels with them, as it says, “Thus says Hashem of Hosts: Though it is wondrous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, it will also be wondrous in My eyes.””

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 14:3: “Likewise Jacob our father, peace be upon him, of whom it is written, ‘You give truth to Jacob,’ and ‘truth is Torah’: of him too we find that he said, ‘The God who has shepherded me from my beginning until this day,’ for he recognized that everything is from Hashem and attributed nothing at all to his own effort. So it is taught (Bereishis Rabbah, beginning of Vayeitzei) that he said of himself, ‘“From where will my help come?” I do not give up my hope in my Creator.’ The name Mattisyahu points to this as well: everything is a free gift, mattas, from Hashem, as the letters Yud-Heh-Vav allude. The name Yochanan points to it too: Yud-Vav chanan, for the Holy One, blessed be He, is the One who grants grace.”
